item.title: ‘A win the size of Texas’: Democrats celebrate shrinking Republican dominance in a big state
item.description:

  • US midterms 2026 live – latest updates

“This is amazing,” exclaimed Tiffany Dunsmore, 44, the owner of Austin Scavenger Hunt, as the city skyline gleamed in the distance on a balmy night. “I cannot believe Texas went blue!”

For 32 long years, turning Texas blue had been an elusive prize for Democrats in the US’s second biggest state. There were false dawns, nearly men and broken dreams. But on Tuesday the party’s agony finally came to an end.

The Democrats have taken control of the Senate and the House of Representatives. These charts and maps reveal the key trends and races behind this result

The Republicans have lost seven Senators, 25 House districts and five governor races.

As of 8.00am Eastern Time (ET) on Wednesday, more than 1,800 of nearly 2,500 counties with Senate elections had returned more than 90% of their votes. Americans did not turn out in significant numbers for the Republicans amid high fuel prices and dissatisfaction with the president.
